aboutH2: Portage Atlantic: Residential Youth Addiction Treatment at Cassidy Lake, New Brunswick
intro: Portage Atlantic is a Non-Profit rehab located in Cassidy Lake, New Brunswick. Portage Atlantic specializes in the treatment of substance, drug and alcohol abuse.

The centre has taken young people aged 14 to 21 since 1996, from New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island and Newfoundland and Labrador. It is free for New Brunswick residents and runs in English and French. Treatment follows the therapeutic community model, where residents live, study and do group work together.

pillars.title: A Campus on the Shore of Cassidy Lake
pillars.body: The centre sits on the shore of Cassidy Lake off Route 865, in the Norton area of Kings County, about 25 minutes from Sussex and under an hour from Saint John. The campus has a main residence with lounges that look out over the water, a dining hall, classrooms and a computer room, plus a gymnasium and a fitness room. A Recovery Trail loops through the woods. In summer residents swim, kayak and fish off the dock, and outings during the year include museums, orchards and community events.

pillars.title: Eighteen Months of Aftercare
pillars.body: Planning for home starts at admission. Over the stay, outings grow from a few hours to whole weekends, and near the end of the residential phase youth can spend up to four days a week back at home. Before they finish, each young person has a plan for where they will live, what they will do for school or work and how they will handle setbacks. Aftercare then usually runs for about 18 months, with group sessions, a social reintegration counsellor and intensive weekends back at Cassidy Lake in the first months. Graduates who go on to post-secondary school can apply for a Portage Atlantic bursary.

pillars.title: Peers, Counsellors and Teachers
pillars.body: Portage runs on the therapeutic community model, so the other residents are part of the treatment. Youth take on shared responsibilities, work in groups and act as role models for newer arrivals, with counsellors guiding each personal plan. Lisa Portelli is the Centre Director. Teachers from the New Brunswick Department of Education and Early Childhood Development run the on-site school, and classes are mandatory for anyone without a high school diploma. Accreditation Canada noted that many Portage staff are former program participants. Families get weekly support groups and one-on-one meetings with a counsellor.

overview: Portage Atlantic is a live-in program for teenagers and young adults with substance use problems, including those who also struggle with their mental health. A stay usually lasts 3 to 6 months, depending on each young person's needs and readiness. Admission is voluntary, nobody needs a referral, and an admission counsellor meets each applicant first to see whether the residential program is a good fit.

afterOverview: Portage Atlantic is part of Portage, a non-profit that also runs youth and adult programs in Quebec. In Greater Moncton, its Moncton Community Care Program offers free short-term support for youth aged 14 to 21 and their families, including help getting ready for live-in treatment at Cassidy Lake. The Portage Atlantic Foundation raises part of the program's funding through donations and events.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Portage Atlantic cost?
faqs.a: The program is free for New Brunswick residents, paid for by the Government of New Brunswick and Portage's partners. Youth from Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island and Newfoundland and Labrador are welcome, and Portage asks them to contact the centre about costs.

Portage Atlantic is for young people aged 14 to 21 who are living with a substance use disorder. It takes youth from all four Atlantic provinces. Recovery.com lists co-occurring mental health conditions among what the centre treats.
The residential program usually lasts 3 to 6 months. Portage sets the length for each young person based on their needs, motivation and readiness. About 18 months of aftercare follow.

faqs.q: How do I get admitted, and do I need a referral?
faqs.a: No referral is needed, and admission is voluntary. Anyone can apply by calling 506-839-1200 or the toll-free line, 1-888-735-9800. An admission counsellor then meets the young person to look at their needs and motivation and decide whether the residential program fits.

faqs.q: Can my child keep going to school?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre has an on-site school run by teachers from the New Brunswick Department of Education and Early Childhood Development. Classes are part-time and mandatory for youth without a high school diploma, and students can take the Canadian Adult Education Credential course (formerly the GED).

faqs.q: Is the program in English or French?
faqs.a: Both. Portage Atlantic runs a bilingual program, offered in English and in French.

Family visits usually start after three weeks of therapy and increase as the resident progresses. Outings grow from a few hours to whole weekends, and near the end of the stay up to four days a week at home. Parents can also join weekly family support groups and meet one-on-one with a counsellor.

No. Recovery.com lists detox as not offered, so the centre does not provide medical withdrawal management. If a young person needs supervised withdrawal first, arrange it through a doctor or hospital and ask Portage about timing for admission.

faqs.q: Where is Portage Atlantic and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Portage Atlantic is at 1275 Route 865 in Cassidy Lake, near Sussex in the Norton area of Kings County, New Brunswick. It is about 50 minutes from Saint John and an hour and a quarter from Moncton by car. Mail goes to P.O. Box 339, Norton, NB E5T 1J7.

faqs.q: What happens after a young person leaves?
faqs.a: Aftercare usually lasts about 18 months in three phases. It includes group sessions, one-on-one support from a social reintegration counsellor and, in the first months, intensive weekends back at Cassidy Lake. Graduates who go on to post-secondary studies can apply for a Portage Atlantic bursary.

Yes. Portage was awarded Accreditation with Commendation by Accreditation Canada in June 2025. The surveyors pointed to how much clients and families are involved in planning care and to staff with lived experience.

Yes. Portage Atlantic's Moncton Community Care Program offers free, short-term support for youth aged 14 to 21 and their families, with no referral needed. It includes needs assessments, groups, workshops and sessions that prepare youth for live-in treatment. Call 506-383-7328.
